source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Perform the intervention once because a provider's request temporarily expands the RN's legal scope when the client needs the service.","B":"Perform the intervention if another RN agrees to observe because peer presence converts an out-of-scope activity into authorized nursing practice.","C":"Do not perform the out-of-scope intervention; clarify and escalate the request through appropriate channels and follow current law and facility policy.","D":"Delegate the intervention to assistive personnel because delegation transfers the legal scope restriction from the RN to the person receiving the task."}}
source_row.rationale: NCSBN identifies practice within legal scope and recognition of professional limitations as Management of Care responsibilities. Option C is the only response that preserves legal scope while using appropriate organizational channels to resolve the client's care need. A provider request or peer observation does not expand statutory scope, and an RN cannot delegate an intervention that is outside the RN's own authorized scope to assistive personnel.

source_row.stem: An RN is asked to perform an intervention that the nurse knows is outside the RN's legal scope of practice in the jurisdiction. Which action is most appropriate?
